channel.title: Vetro guides
channel.description: Samsung Tizen TV guides from the Vetro project.

item.title: How to root a Samsung TV (Tizen): what works in 2026
item.description: How rooting a Samsung Tizen TV works today: what root means and does not give you, which TVs have reports from 2018 to 2024, the risks and the research.

item.title: Root a Tizen 6 Samsung TV (2021): models and firmware
item.description: 2021 Samsung TVs run Tizen 6. Four are reported working with Vetro (Q80A, Q70A, Q60A, QN85A); an AU7000 report failed at the root agent. Firmware and caveats.

item.title: Root a 2022 Samsung TV (Tizen 6.5): models and firmware
item.description: 2022 Samsung TVs run Tizen 6.5. Five models have Vetro reports (Q67B, BU8002, QN85B, S95B, The Frame), the Home cache fix and what stayed unconfirmed.

item.title: Root a 2023 Samsung TV (Tizen 7+): what owners reported
item.description: 2023 Samsung TVs launched on Tizen 7. Owners reported Vetro on the S90C, Q65S95C and CU7179, with an installer caveat and one set that lists Tizen 9.0.

item.title: Root a 2024 Samsung TV (Tizen 8, 9): what is confirmed
item.description: What is confirmed for 2024 Samsung TVs on Tizen 8 and 9: Q65D and S90D owner reports, failed Tizen 9 and 10 reports, a 2023 CU7179 and outside research.

item.title: Root a 2019 or 2020 Samsung TV (Tizen 5): what works
item.description: Root features need Tizen 6 or newer. A 2019 Q80R works with a local port; the 2020 TU7090 and T4300 and a 2018 NU7090 get the dashboard only, no root.

item.title: Samsung TV Tizen version by year, 2017 to 2026
item.description: Which Tizen version a Samsung TV shipped with, year by year from 2017 to 2026, why your TV may run a newer one now, and how the version relates to rooting.

item.title: How to enable Developer Mode on a Samsung TV
item.description: Turn on Samsung TV Developer Mode: open Apps, enter 12345, switch it on, type the host IP and restart. Fixes for a remote that will not take the code.

item.title: Is it safe to root a Samsung TV? Risks and what to undo
item.description: Rooting a Samsung TV carries boot, network and update risks. See the documented Q80A boot hazard, open dashboard, plugin trust and what Restore can undo.

item.title: Connect to a Samsung TV with sdb (port 26101)
item.description: How to run sdb connect to a Samsung TV on port 26101, why sdb shell is often closed on retail firmware, and how Vetro 0.5.0 uses the TV's own SDB with no PC.

item.title: Install Vetro on a Samsung TV with Apps2Samsung
item.description: Step by step: Developer Mode, Apps2Samsung, the root package, pairing, Host PC IP 127.0.0.1 and a restart, then the Vetro dashboard on port 8099.

item.title: Samsung TV certificate errors when installing an app
item.description: Why a sideloaded app fails on a Samsung TV: author vs distributor certificates, the DUID, a leftover build with another certificate, account and DNS blocks.

item.title: Does root survive a restart on a Samsung TV?
item.description: What happens to Samsung TV root after a restart, standby, a full power cycle or a firmware update, and how Vetro gets root back by itself in up to 90 seconds.

item.title: Uninstall Vetro from a Samsung TV and clean up leftovers
item.description: Remove Vetro from a Samsung TV: restore its changes first, delete the app, turn Developer Mode off, and know what a plain uninstall leaves behind on the TV.

item.title: Turn off ACR on a Samsung TV: menu steps and limits
item.description: Disable ACR on a Samsung TV with the Viewing Information Services switch, see what it leaves running, a 2026 opt-out test, and extra blocking on rooted TVs.

item.title: Samsung ACR Texas settlement: consent rules explained
item.description: Texas sued five TV makers over ACR in December 2025, won then lost a restraining order against Samsung, and settled in February 2026. Dates, terms and limits.

item.title: What data does a Samsung TV collect? A plain inventory
item.description: What a Samsung TV collects according to Samsung's own notices: viewing data, advertising IDs, voice, usage logs and location, and where each setting lives.

item.title: Block Samsung TV telemetry with Pi-hole or AdGuard
item.description: Which Samsung domains community Pi-hole lists block, what breaks, why some TVs bypass your DNS, and the on-TV DNS blocking in Vetro. Limits and breakage risks.

item.title: Turn off Bixby, Alexa and the mic on a Samsung TV
item.description: How to disable Bixby and Alexa on a Samsung TV: the hardware mic switch on some models, Voice Wake-up, the Voice menu, and what Vetro's voice switch does.

item.title: Samsung TV ads opt-out: turn off interest-based ads
item.description: Turn off Interest-Based Advertisements on a Samsung TV, reset the advertising ID, and learn what Samsung's notices say you will still see. Menu paths vary.

item.title: Remove ads from the Samsung TV home screen: your options
item.description: Can you remove ads from the Samsung TV home screen? What the menus allow, what DNS blocking leaves behind, and how a launcher on a rooted TV replaces Home.

item.title: Remove Samsung TV Plus from a Samsung TV: what works
item.description: Samsung says TV Plus can't be fully removed. See the channel and tile steps on its support pages, and what Vetro's Task manager documents on a rooted TV.

item.title: Samsung TV slow? Restart, cache and network fixes
item.description: Samsung TV slow or lagging? Cold boot, clear app cache, check the network and update before a Smart Hub reset, plus one memory figure for rooted TVs.

item.title: Samsung TV memory usage: what uses RAM and how to read it
item.description: What uses memory on a Samsung TV: available versus used RAM, zram and swap, and the sizes Vetro's notes record for Samsung Home, HbbTV and Ambient on a Q80A.

item.title: Custom launcher for Samsung TV: how it replaces Home
item.description: How a custom launcher replaces Samsung's Home on a rooted Tizen TV: the Home key, what Vetro's native launcher does, one memory figure and its beta limits.

item.title: Stop Samsung TV automatic firmware updates: options
item.description: How to turn off Samsung TV Auto Update, what Samsung says keeps installing anyway, what router blocking does, and what Vetro's switch changes on a rooted TV.

item.title: Can you downgrade Samsung TV firmware? What reports say
item.description: Samsung says downgrading TV firmware is not supported. See what its community and SamyGO threads report, and why Vetro offers prevention, not a rollback.

item.title: Will a Samsung TV firmware update remove root? What we know
item.description: Can a firmware update remove root on a Samsung TV? What the root research and Vetro's public records say, what to do before updating, and what is unknown.

item.title: Remap Samsung remote buttons (Netflix, Prime and more)
item.description: Samsung gives no setting to change the Netflix or Prime Video button. What the stock TV allows and how Vetro's Remapper reassigns keys on a rooted TV.

item.title: Home Assistant Samsung TV: three ways to connect it
item.description: Connect a Samsung TV to Home Assistant with the built-in integration, a community fork, or MQTT from the TV itself. What each does, needs and cannot do.

item.title: Samsung TV remote buttons as Home Assistant events
item.description: Home Assistant can send keys to a Samsung TV but cannot hear its remote. Here is how a rooted TV running Vetro can publish a button press over MQTT.

item.title: Jellyfin on a Samsung TV: official app or sideloading
item.description: Jellyfin reached Samsung's app store in February 2026 for some TVs. If yours is not eligible, here is how sideloading works and why it needs no root.

item.title: TizenTube on Samsung TV: install steps and requirements
item.description: How to install TizenTube on a Samsung Tizen TV with Developer Mode and Apps2Samsung, which build to pick, the proxy DNS prerequisite and common errors.

item.title: Vetro vs AeroTizen, free-my-tv and TizenBrew
item.description: Vetro, AeroTizen, free-my-tv and TizenBrew compared on root, install route, what each changes on a Samsung TV, and who should pick which.

item.title: Rooted Samsung TV vs streaming box: which one to choose
item.description: A debloated, rooted Samsung TV or a Fire TV, Google TV or Apple TV box? Compared on ads, privacy, updates and effort. Neither route removes every ad.

item.title: Samsung TV model number decoder: model code and firmware
item.description: Read a Samsung TV model number letter by letter, from QE50Q80AATXZT to the year letter, and learn what a firmware string like T-NKM2DEUC-2301.1 can tell you.

item.title: What each Vetro switch changes on a Samsung TV (0.5.0)
item.description: What each Vetro 0.5.0 Quick settings switch, Launcher option and Task manager action changes on a Samsung TV, how to undo it, and what is untested.

item.title: Vetro security model: pairing, plain HTTP, trusted LAN
item.description: Vetro 0.5.0 pairs browsers with a six-digit code shown on the TV, but traffic stays plain HTTP. What pairing covers, what stays open, SDB, plugins, reports.

item.title: Why Vetro's launcher is native, not a web app
item.description: Why Vetro's Samsung TV launcher is a native .NET program, not a web app: the memory numbers from one Q80A run, how the Home key works, and what native costs.
